Cecilia Peterson December 9, 2021 Get our Newsletter! Get our Newsletter! My grandpa Harold, uncle Curt, cousin Eric, grandma Lucille, and cousin Nils at Christmas in the early 1980s. People were confused whenever I asked about it.” Now, I don’t believe most people speak so casually about obscure sausage varieties, but Kat happens to have made potatis korv with me for years, in preparation for my annual Christmas smörgåsbord . I’ve never been to Sweden myself, despite exactly half of my ancestors claiming Swedish heritage. Still, it surprised me—I can’t remember a year in my life where my Grandma Lucille laid out the smörgåsbord and the korv was missing. pages.text: Leonardo's horse took 500 years to make | National Geographic Published April 30, 2019 • 2 min read Studies of horses drawn by Leonardo da Vinci circa 1490, when he was planning “Il Gran Cavallo.” Collection of the Royal Library, Windsor Castle, Windsor, England Photograph by Print Collector/Album At the request of Ludovico Sforza, the future Duke of Milan , Leonardo da Vinci began working on a sculpture that would be the largest equestrian statue in the world in 1482. Leonardo made sketches of the horses in the Sforza stables, from which he designed a 24-foot-high clay model. Leonardo wanted to cast the horse in a single operation and designed elaborate plaster molds to make that possible. In his innovative process, the inverted molds would be buried between two ovens, and molten bronze would fill them to cast the statue. War versus art The plans were set to create the giant horse, but war with France engulfed Milan in 1499. Sforza needed the bronze for weapons, not art, and the materials were diverted to forge cannons. The French defeated Milan, occupied Sforza's lands, and destroyed the clay horse. Leonardo ’s drawings and plans survived, but the artist died in May 1519 before “Il Gran Cavallo” could be brought to life. pages.text: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says there are no trust issues between himself and team - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Lewis Hamilton is fourth in the 2026 F1 drivers' championship By Andrew Benson F1 Correspondent Published 4 hours ago Lewis Hamilton says there is "definitely not" a trust problem between him and his Ferrari team. The seven-time champion has twice in the past four races ignored a call to pit for fresh tyres, both times to his competitive disadvantage. The most recent time, in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix on 8 November, Hamilton stayed out on worn slick tyres in worsening rain and ended up spinning before pitting on the next lap. Before this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, Hamilton spoke positively of his relationship with his race engineer Carlo Santi. "We're constantly working on our communication," said Hamilton, who had a different race engineer last year. "It's been a lot better this year. Carlos (sic) has done an amazing job. And those particular two times, particularly the last time, was just I didn't have the information I needed. I got the call right at the last minute. "We'll just continue to work on the processes. We're super united in what's working, in the right direction." The previous time Hamilton ignored a call to pit was in Singapore, when he decided to stay out during a virtual safety car period. pages.text: Lewis Moody: England team to support MND challenge at All Blacks match - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Moody spoke to England's players in the dressing room after last November's win over Australia, shortly after revealing his MND diagnosis By Mike Henson BBC Sport rugby union news reporter Published 17 November 2026 Lewis Moody says he has been buoyed by the England team's support as he launches his latest challenge in aid of Motor Neurone Disease (MND) research at Saturday's match against New Zealand at Allianz Stadium. England will wear training tops and specially-painted boots publicising Moody's 'Front Up' campaign, which is calling on supporters to converge on the British coastline in June for a day of fundraising walks. "I just couldn't be more grateful to the team, the lads that have been in touch and the energy and excitement they have wanted to bring to this," said Moody. "To have their buy-in is wonderful for me. It speaks to the connection the rugby family has, whatever the team, the era, the nationality, and the strength of that bond." Moody, who won 71 England caps, was part of the 2003 Rugby World Cup-winning side and captained the team at the 2011 tournament. He was diagnosed with MND last year. The muscle-wasting condition impacted the lives of Doddie Weir, the former Scotland and British and Irish Lions second row, and rugby league star Rob Burrow in recent years. Both have since died. Close lhirlimann's Diary Capitole du Libre 2026 Posted by lhirlimann on 15 November 2026 in French (Français) . Hier soir, j’ai présenté dans l’amphithéâtre C002 au sein du campus de enseeiht à Toulouse, « Contribuez à OSM ». La bonne surprise fut le taux de remplissage de la salle. J’ai compté plus d’une vingtaine de personnes. La présentation était articulée en deux parties : la première, un tout petit peu de théorie et pas de présentation d’outils ; la deuxième, des démonstrations, des petits trucs faciles pour commencer, puis des trucs plus « grands » (de l’infrastructure). En trente minutes, j’avais plié ma présentation. Il restait vingt-cinq minutes, qui se sont très, très facilement remplies par de très nombreuses questions. Merci au plublic pour ces questions. Merci à l’organisation du Capitole du Libre. La présentation est disponible à https://files.hirlimann.net/talks/cdl2026/ . Library and information science is a field of study that encompasses all of the aspects of the creation, organization, documentation, management, communication, and use of recorded information. It is the umbrella term for a wide variety of fields of study and work, including librarianship, information management, knowledge management, archiving, and records management, and is tangential to museum studies. pages.text: Libya oil refinery fire: Firefighters battle huge blaze after drone attack Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Libyan authorities battle big blaze at major oil refinery 11 August 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Basillioh Rukanga Watch: Huge blaze after attack on petrol tank in Libya Libyan emergency services have been battling to contain a huge blaze at a major oil plant after it was targeted by unknown attackers. The Zawiya refinery, west of the capital Tripoli, was hit in a drone strike on Monday evening - the third such incident in two days. The National Oil Corporation (NOC) said a tank containing about 4.5m litres of fuel was directly hit, triggering a huge fire that caused it to collapse. It said it was considering suspending operations if the attacks continued. There were no "serious injuries" from the fire, with most patients treated for smoke inhalation, Libya's Ambulance and Emergency Service said on Tuesday. The Zawiya refinery is the largest operational facility in Libya, with an output of 120,000 barrels per day. The NOC condemned similar attacks in past days in Zawiya, including two drone strikes on a naphtha reservoir and a water desalination plant. It called on the authorities to investigate who was behind the violence. The attacks have highlighted continuing instability in Libya, which has been split in two since a civil war broke out after the ousting of former leader Muammar Gaddafi. I could finally relax," says Abdulwahab Damdoum, surveying his luxurious new apartment overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, in the eastern Libyan city of Derna. Just three years ago he was clinging in terror to the roof of a house as the world's deadliest flood this century surged around him. Now the 27-year-old port worker, his wife and two young daughters have been given a new, free, 300-sq-m home in a showcase development commissioned by a son of Khalifa Haftar, the warlord who controls eastern Libya. It is part of a rapid $2bn (£1.5bn) rebuilding of Derna that the powerful Haftar family hope will serve as a model for development throughout Libya, increasing their influence across a country currently split between east and west, with rival governments in charge. The money comes from the state coffers of the oil-rich country, allocated by its parliament. But there are no published records of how it has been spent, raising questions about accountability and possible corruption. pages.text: Light pollution is getting worse, and Earth is paying the price | National Geographic By Nadia Drake Photographs by Babak Tafreshi Published April 3, 2019 • 25 min read On a clear night in 1994, an earthquake rumbled beneath Los Angeles and caused a city-wide power outage just before dawn. Startled awake, some residents who had stumbled outside called various emergency centers and a local observatory to report a mysterious cloud overhead. That weird object turned out to be the band of the Milky Way , our home galaxy, which had long been obscured from view by the city’s lights. Arguably, the light bulb is the most transformative invention humans have introduced to this planet. By flicking a switch or pushing a button, we can push back the veil that would naturally shroud our lives each night. Now, we work long after the sun sinks below the horizon. We play games outside until the hours stretch into double digits. We more safely roam city streets after dark. ( Opinion: Bright Nights, Big Problems) The city of Las Vegas dumps an enormous amount of light into its environment, turning the night sky above into a seemingly blank canvas. Light Water Reactor Sustainability (LWRS) Program The Light Water Reactor Sustainability (LWRS) program conducts research to develop technologies and other solutions to improve the economics and reliability, sustain the safety, and extend the operation of our nation’s fleet of nuclear power plants. It has two objectives with respect to long-term operations: (1) to provide science- and technology-based solutions to industry to overcome the current labor-intensive business model and associated practices; and (2) to manage the aging of systems, structures, and components (SSCs) so nuclear power plants can continue to operate safely and cost-effectively. The Light Water Reactor Sustainability (LWRS) program is focused on the following three goals: Developing the fundamental scientific basis to understand, predict, and measure changes in materials and SSCs as they age in environments associated with continued long-term operations of existing nuclear power plants. Here’s everything you need to know about lightning, from how it forms to common myths and how to stay safe. Lightning flashes during a tropical storm in Guatemala. Photograph By Babak Tafreshi, Nat Geo Image Collection By National Geographic Staff Last updated July 21, 2025 Lightning flashing across a darkened sky makes an unforgettable image. With their drama and power, it’s no wonder people have infused them with symbolic meaning. They’re associated with mythological deities, such as Zeus and Thor, and even an emoji , in popular culture. In daily life, these electric currents can be dangerous, sparking intense forest fires and causing deaths. It doesn’t help that there are many myths about lightning behavior. From its causes to safety tips, here’s everything you need to know about these bolts from the blue. What is lightning and what causes it? Lightning is an electrical discharge caused by imbalances between storm clouds and the ground, or within the clouds themselves. Most occur within the clouds. During a storm, colliding particles of rain, ice, or snow inside storm clouds increase the imbalance between storm clouds and the ground, and often negatively charge the lower reaches of storm clouds. ( Summer storms can strike suddenly. Here’s what causes them .) Objects on the ground, like steeples, trees, and Earth itself, become positively charged. Lili Colon Lili Colon, Chief Technology Officer With more than 20 years of experience, Lili Colón has a deep understanding of how quickly the threat landscape changes and what is needed to best secure and protect the U.S. energy infrastructure. pages.text: Lillygol Sedaghat sees trash as a precious commodity | National Geographic Photograph by Rebecca Hale, NGM staff SCIENCE PLANET OR PLASTIC? She sees trash as a precious commodity ‘Our trash doesn’t disappear, it goes somewhere’—and in a circular economy, it could be a valuable resource, says this environmentalist. By Annie Roth Published November 7, 2019 • 3 min read This story appears in the December 2019 issue of National Geographic magazine. Banana peels and plastic straws are little more than garbage in most of the world. To environmental educator Lillygol Sedaghat , they’re precious commodities. For the past two years, the 27-year-old National Geographic explorer has traveled the globe to advocate for the untapped potential of trash. The linear economy, where resources are turned into disposable products, “is no longer sustainable,” Sedaghat says. She aims to promote a circular economy, in which “you maximize your resources and minimize your waste.” Since 2017 Sedaghat has researched one of the world’s most efficient waste management systems: Taiwan recycles nearly half its municipal waste and has reduced the amount sent to landfills to less than one percent—turning plastic waste into cell phone cases and food scraps into fertilizer. To Sedaghat, it’s a prime example of how a zero-waste economy can work. Her goal? pages.title: List of Goods Produced by Child Labor or Forced Labor | U.S. Department of Labor
pages.text: List of Goods Produced by Child Labor or Forced Labor | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content List of Goods Produced by Child Labor or Forced Labor The Bureau of International Labor Affairs (ILAB) maintains a list of goods and their source countries which it has reason to believe are produced by child labor or forced labor in violation of international standards, as required under the Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act (TVPRA) of 2005 and subsequent reauthorizations. The List of Goods Produced by Child Labor or Forced Labor comprises 204 goods from 82 countries and areas, as of September 5, 2024. The Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Prevention and Protection Reauthorization Act of 2018 directs that the List include, "to the extent practicable, goods that are produced with inputs that are produced with forced labor or child labor." ILAB maintains the List primarily to raise public awareness about forced labor and child labor around the world and to promote efforts to combat them; it is not intended to be punitive, but rather to serve as a catalyst for more strategic and focused coordination and collaboration among those working to address these problems. Introduction Lithium batteries are vital components in many everyday consumer products, such as cell phones and backup power storage units. They play a crucial role in the rapidly growing U.S. markets for vehicle manufacturing, energy storage, medical services, and agricultural technology. These batteries also may contain important minerals and materials, including lithium (Li), cobalt (Co), and nickel (Ni), which are essential for many technologies driving U.S. commerce. Credit: Megan King/NIST Four years ago, NIST researcher Cyrus Daugherty developed an algorithm to virtually unroll the tightly wrapped layers of a cylindrical lithium-ion battery. Daugherty’s software transformed X-ray images of the battery, taken at different angles, into a CT scan. The scan, a 3D portrait of the battery’s interior, pinpointed hard-to-spot defects and highlighted wear and tear on its electrodes. This study aims to extend the life of lithium-ion batteries , which power everything from laptops and cellphones to e-bikes and electric cars. LM Information Technology Specialist Kyle Brown accepted the award on LM’s behalf. The EPEAT award recognizes organizations for excellence in sustainable procurement of electronic equipment. EPEAT is a method for purchasers to evaluate a product’s effect on the environment, rate it accordingly, and identify it as a preferable electronic good. Manufacturers register products in the EPEAT category based on the device’s ability to meet certain criteria, including product lifestyle, design, energy production, and recycling. pages.text: Lobito Corridor: Can Trump-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo and Angola? Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo? 3 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Akisa Wandera BBC Africa, Lobito AFP via Getty Images The Lobito Corridor links DR Congo's mineral-rich south to Angola's Atlantic coast through the Benguela Railway and the Port of Lobito As trains carrying thousands of tonnes of copper from the Democratic Republic of Congo roar through her community, 20-year-old Manuela Julia is not thinking about critical minerals or billion-dollar investments. She is thinking about getting around more easily. The railway runs through Catumbela, near the Angolan city of Lobito, on the Atlantic coast. For Julia, it has made travelling cheaper and more convenient. "Before, I had to use a taxi, which is much more expensive. Now it is cheaper and easier to travel," she says. But the railway has ambitions far bigger than improving local transport. It is part of the Lobito Corridor, a US-backed effort to secure access to Africa's critical minerals and promote regional economic cooperation, which Washington hopes will help bring peace to conflict-torn eastern DR Congo. Some 550 people watched a King's Lynn and West Norfolk Borough Council meeting on Monday, which was also livestreamed, to discuss the infrastructure projects near King's Lynn, Norfolk. The Longmarsh Green Energy (LGE) developments would cover 4,695 acres (1,900 hectares) of farmland across two sites. A spokesperson said it would "make an important contribution" to energy systems and supporting online networks. The council opposed the scheme's approval. However, owing to the development's scale, it will be deemed a nationally significant infrastructure project, which means its approval will rest with the government rather than the local authority.
